hints: Think about the lock and key idea for enzymes, what is it that has to fit precisely into the active site?
Glucokinase is named for glucose, so ask yourself whether it would work just as well on lots of different sugars or only on glucose and very similar molecules.
Separate the conditions an enzyme needs to work well from the actual molecules it chooses to work on, then pick the statement about choice of substrate.
walkthrough:
**Recall what specificity means**

Think of specificity as pickiness. An enzyme does not catalyse every reaction, it picks out only one substrate shape, or a very small family of similar shapes, that fit its active site.

Think: lock accepts only the right key.

**Separate specificity from optimum conditions**

Many enzymes work best only in a narrow pH range or at a narrow temperature range. That is called the optimum pH or optimum temperature, and it is about denaturation and rate, not about specificity.

**Separate specificity from general catalyst action**

All catalysts, including enzymes, speed up a reaction by providing an alternative route of lower activation energy. That is true for glucokinase, but it is not what the word specificity describes.

**Apply to glucokinase**

Glucokinase is involved in glucose metabolism because its active site is shaped to bind glucose. Specificity means it will only operate on glucose or a very narrow range of very similar substrate molecules, not on any molecule that happens to be present.

options.A: This describes optimum pH, not specificity. It is true that enzymes are sensitive to pH, but being most effective over a narrow pH range does not explain why glucokinase picks glucose rather than another substrate.
options.B: This describes optimum temperature, not specificity. Enzymes do have a narrow temperature range before they denature, but that tells you about conditions for activity, not about which substrate molecules are accepted.
options.C: This is the definition of specificity. The active site of glucokinase is complementary to glucose, so it only binds and catalyses reactions of glucose or a very narrow range of closely related substrates.
options.D: This describes how all catalysts work, by providing an alternative pathway of lower activation energy. It applies to glucokinase and to inorganic catalysts, so it does not define what makes an enzyme specific.
